title: USMNT’s Gio Reyna in talks over move to Strasbourg from Borussia Monchengladbach
author: Paul Tenorio
content:
U.S. men’s national team midfielder Gio Reyna is in talks about a potential move to Strasbourg from Borussia Monchengladbach, sources briefed on the situation tell The Athletic.

The 23-year-old has been with Gladbach for just one season, making 19 Bundesliga appearances and scoring one goal. Reyna, the son of U.S. men’s national team legend Claudio Reyna, may be joining his fourth club in as many seasons should the proposed move to France advance.

Strasbourg finished eighth in Ligue 1 last season. The team is owned by BlueCo, the consortium led by U.S. businessman Todd Boehly and Clearlake Capital, which bought Chelsea in 2022 and made Strasbourg part of its multi-club model a year later.

Reyna has struggled to get on the field consistently in recent seasons due to injuries that have plagued his career. He played just over 500 Bundesliga minutes in 2025-26, continuing a trend in which the attacking midfielder has failed to log more than 625 minutes in league play since 2020-21, when he was still a teenager breaking out for Borussia Dortmund.

He moved to Gladbach from Dortmund in the summer of 2025 in search of regular minutes ahead of the 2026 World Cup.

Despite his lack of playing time at the club level, U.S. men’s national team coach Mauricio Pochettino brought Reyna to the World Cup, declaring him a “very special talent.” Reyna rewarded his coach with a late trivela goal in a 4-1 win over Paraguay, but otherwise struggled to make an impact. He played in all five games for the U.S., clocking 131 minutes, including a 75-minute start against Turkey, and registered just one shot after his goal.

Reyna was once seen as the best prospect in the U.S. player pool and a complement to winger Christian Pulisic.

He played 1,976 minutes for Dortmund in 2020-21, scoring four goals with five assists, adding another three goals in the DFB-Pokal and an assist in the Champions League. Muscle injuries, though, halted that progress.

The former New York City FC academy prospect produced for the national team when he was healthy, however. Reyna scored in a 3-2 Concacaf Nations League final win over Mexico and was named to the 2022 World Cup team. He became embroiled in controversy there when he was nearly sent home for disciplinary issues after learning he would not start the World Cup opener against Wales.

Reyna eventually played 52 minutes in four games at the tournament. A controversy between his parents and former U.S. coach Gregg Berhalter erupted after the tournament, but Reyna remained involved in the national team picture.

He had two assists in the 2023 Concacaf Nations League final and a further two in the 2024 Nations League semifinal and a goal in the final, earning best player of the tournament honors.
